problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:

* Component Alpha: size 66 cubic meters
* Component Beta: size 31 cubic meters
* Component Gamma: size 45 cubic meters
* Component Delta: size 67 cubic meters
* Component Epsilon: size 30 cubic meters
* Component Zeta: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Eta: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Theta: size 51 cubic meters
* Component Iota: size 35 cubic meters
* Component Kappa: size 66 cubic meters
* Component Lambda: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Mu: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Nu: size 34 cubic meters
* Component Xi: size 56 cubic meters
* Component Omicron: size 42 cubic meters
* Component Pi: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Rho: size 66 cubic meters
* Component Sigma: size 46 cubic meters
* Component Tau: size 39 cubic meters
* Component Upsilon: size 43 cubic meters
* Component Phi: size 63 cubic meters
* Component Chi: size 41 cubic meters
* Component Psi: size 68 cubic meters
* Component Omega: size 38 cubic meters
* Component Ares: size 62 cubic meters
* Component Zeus: size 37 cubic meters
* Component Hera: size 50 cubic meters
* Component Poseidon: size 67 cubic meters
* Component Apollo: size 67 cubic meters
* Component Athena: size 65 cubic meters
* Component Hermes: size 70 cubic meters
* Component Dionysus: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Artemis: size 36 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of freight. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume in a plane cannot exceed its capacity.
